requirements.requirement: node2 (lan-a) can reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: A single pf pass rule was added on node1 restricting source to the lan-a network (vtnet1:network) and destination to node3's specific address 10.60.2.2 port 8080 (cmd-56d11f544df5449f, cmd-9ddfef07a276480f). node3's firewalld also had to be opened for 8080/tcp (cmd-7e970e97a0b64e3d) since it independently blocked the port. Functional curl test from node2 to node3:8080 returned HTTP 200 (cmd-115fd0df8fb34932), and this was re-verified after all three node restarts (cmd-2092535544b04fa0, cmd-7449c094b1c744a6, cmd-5269adeed1134460).

requirements.requirement: Every other flow between lan-a and lan-b remains refused (default-deny preserved)
requirements.summary: After opening the single rule, tests directly from node2 showed ping to node3 fails, TCP/22 to node3 is blocked, TCP/9090 to node3 times out, and node3->node2:8080 (reverse direction) also times out, all consistent with default-deny (cmd-7ab49b8819374fb8, cmd-bc3a7bad9f614ce7). The same negative tests (ping, port 9090) were repeated after node3's restart and still failed (cmd-5269adeed1134460), confirming the narrow scope held.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 correctly addressed/routed on lan-a/lan-b so the intended path is even reachable
requirements.summary: node1's opt1 (vtnet1, 10.60.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.60.2.1/24) were assigned via config.xml and configctl (cmd-f8df3d85073d4ee6, cmd-b376e41283c7498a). node2 and node3 were given persistent static IPs (10.60.1.2/24, 10.60.2.2/24) and static routes to the peer subnet via nmcli profiles, confirmed to persist and route correctly (cmd-b786928673da4706, cmd-a8cfef54d8b04011, cmd-2f6afc99d2ff4f0b, cmd-fc4239d0640a4f6c).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all three managed nodes with pre/post boot identity and recovered state
requirements.summary: For each node the executor captured a pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity, issued a restart, polled through the outage, observed a changed boot identity, and confirmed recovered configuration and end-to-end functional state. node1: kern.boottime 16:53:37->16:59:44 (cmd-a5438173e2de458d, cmd-d38d80ee6d204c77, cmd-09a1a40a199940fb, cmd-0796dddda90b4d45, cmd-2092535544b04fa0). node2: boot_id 03408ac4->7dbfca00 (cmd-c39c7e8a1d5a4f7d, cmd-8167304d70d54f0f, cmd-38e58d2f8e2d4a95, cmd-7449c094b1c744a6). node3: boot_id 6ab6a71b->c38d5dd9 (cmd-826a2b1b5a334c73, cmd-2de0e70722474dd3, cmd-e6fd679a3b58413f, cmd-12f4a4df651644b1, cmd-5269adeed1134460). These boot identity transitions match the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot cross-check for all three nodes.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the core contract: exactly one TCP/8080 path from node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b) was opened via a single, narrowly-scoped pf rule on node1 (source restricted to lan-a network, destination restricted to node3's specific address), with node3's firewalld also opened for that port. Functional testing directly demonstrated the intended flow works while ping, port 9090, port 22, and the reverse direction all remain refused, both before and after restarting all three nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was thoroughly executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, changed boot identities, and confirmed recovered configuration and end-to-end connectivity, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall, with only minor superseded troubleshooting mutations and leftover temporary test-server log files as residue.
limitations: Some evidence relies on trimmed/truncated command output (e.g., pfctl -sr, config.xml dumps), so full rule sets could not be independently verified beyond the shown fragments.

The before-prepare and after-prepare lifecycle snapshots are identical (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor state separation reduces to a direct before/after-executor comparison only.
Cannot verify from the trace whether the config.xml backup mentioned in the executor's summary was actually created, as no corresponding command was included in the evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were directly tied to the task or its restart-evidence protocol. Two bounded, low-risk troubleshooting mutations occurred before the persisted configuration was applied and were effectively superseded rather than explicitly reverted: a manual `ifconfig vtnet1/vtnet2` IP assignment on node1 (cmd-ae6ac93e690541b5) later replaced by the persisted config.xml/configctl approach, and raw `ip addr add` on node2/node3 (cmd-9b9c9ec2377246cc, cmd-9efd155ca4c44ad3) later replaced by persistent nmcli profiles with the same addressing — no incorrect final state resulted. Several temporary python http.server test listeners were started on node3 to validate reachability across each restart (cmd-983c9b14a80f4088, cmd-bc3a7bad9f614ce7, cmd-b9d9f0d34cb742b8, cmd-12f4a4df651644b1); the final listener process was killed (cmd-e2fab77ddbea4620), but its log/pid files (/tmp/srv.log, srv.pid, srv2.log, srv3.log, srv4.log) remained in the after-executor snapshot as minor residue. tcpdump captures on node1 were read-only diagnostics and were cleanly killed (cmd-1e1653410c584521). No failed services, damaged package state, or weakened security controls were observed in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot.
